# D1 JPEG design fixtures — not supported product examples yet

These assets and the proposed expectations accompany the [D1 design](../../../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-bounded-jpeg-design.md). The current engine still rejects `img`; this directory does not claim otherwise.

All image pixels were authored procedurally for this repository in `scripts/jpeg_fixtures.py`. No external photo, screenshot, user document, or standalone font is included. The colored chart has red/green top corners, blue/yellow bottom corners, an upward arrow and unequal bars to make orientation errors visible. `gray.jpg` is a horizontal grayscale ramp. `odd-420.jpg` exercises partial MCU edges. These repository-authored fixtures follow the repository license; no license terms were changed.

Run `python scripts/jpeg_fixtures.py --check` with Pillow 12.3.0 (fixture-authoring environment JPEG codec compatibility version 6.2, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1). It checks every committed byte hash, decodes the ten proposed positive cases independently, verifies their dimensions/mode/decoded-pixel hash, and records independent decoder behavior for negative cases. It independently checks the complete-symbol/oversubscribed Huffman negative and legal FF fill before DQT/RST/EOI. It deliberately does not decode the over-limit dimension/pixel headers. A tolerant decoder may accept a proposed negative case; that does not make FactsPDF's stricter proposed contract pass or fail.

`--generate` is only for deliberate fixture authoring. It rewrites bytes and the authoring manifest; do not run it to repair a failed comparison. Cross-version decoder differences require examination rather than automatic reference replacement. Pillow is a development/verification tool, not a product dependency.

`manifest.json` contains 35 real byte fixtures and proposed loader outcomes. `acceptance-cases.json` separately records 18 proposed conversion cases, six exact loader boundaries and two default-limit execution recipes, with actual applicable entries specified. Four custom-options conversion cases and the custom loader limits apply only to the managed API. The 320×160 chart rendered at 200pt must be 200×100pt, intentionally different from its 240×120pt natural size. `report.html` requires the existing explicitly licensed Latin/CJK font manifest and a resource binding `chart -> rgb-420.jpg`; no font binaries are included.

The manifest's decoded hashes describe these source JPEGs under the recorded independent decoder. They are **not** generated PDF reference images or user-approved page baselines. No D1 output PDF, cross-entry success, performance claim, or page approval exists at this design stage. Remaining malformed bit-level cases, resource/cancellation boundaries and real PDF checks are mandatory implementation work in the linked plan.
